name: X1 (mtDNA)
description: Mitochondrial haplogroup X1 is the Near Eastern and North African subclade of haplogroup X, contrasting with the more famous X2 which has a trans-continental distribution. X1 is found at 3–8% frequencies in North Africa (particularly among Berber populations), the Levant, and the Arabian Peninsula. X1's distribution in North Africa and the Near East suggests it may represent an ancient backflow from the Near East into North Africa, or possibly an in situ diversification in North Africa. X1 is considerably more common than X2 in the Maghreb, making it a significant marker of North African and Near Eastern maternal heritage.
interestingFact: While X2 grabbed scientific headlines for its mysterious presence among Native Americans (seemingly connecting them to European or Near Eastern populations), the less publicized X1 has its own fascinating story as a marker of North African and Near Eastern populations — particularly the Berbers of the Maghreb, who carry X1 at rates 10 times higher than most European populations.
